setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Here Comes Sunshine** (1 review): Reviewer likes Here Comes Sunshine as the opening number [10]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Reviewer calls He's Gone sublime, ranking it among the top few versions [14]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Reviewer hears free-jazz style improvisation during Eyes, driven by the horn section [9]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer praises the brass added in the Weather Report Suite into Let It Grow section [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-09-26.sbd-repatched.miller.80198.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 194 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer considers this a very nice soundboard rendering; Starts of Brown Eyed Women and Around And Around are missing [1][16]
- **gd1973-09-26.sbd.mtx.tobin.82879.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 196 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: The matrix adds audience atmosphere, improved spatial feel and bass, notably on Here Comes Sunshine and Weather Report into Let It Grow; Reviewer finds the matrix mix sounds like it has slapback delay, so prefers the plain soundboard [14][15]
- **gd1973-09-26.aud.tobin.80665.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 25 songs; 196 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: The start of the show through Playing runs about two seconds per minute fast and needed speed correction [4]
- **gd73-09-26.sbd.brame.16155.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 26 songs; 169 min; rated 3.71/5 by 7 [5]. Said about its sound: Audience splices appear in the lineage, and the soundboard portions are described as loose and lacking top end [7]

## Around the show

- Guests Martin Fierro and Joe Ellis, on trumpet and sax, add horns to the Eyes into Weather Report Suite stretch of set two [7]
- The horn section pushes the band further than usual throughout the show [9]
- Reviewer says the second set is the stronger one and the first set is weaker [16]
- Reviewer says the second set is the stronger one and the first set is weaker [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-09-26.sbd-repatched.miller.80198.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (48k) DSBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (48k) D [1]. Also: Audience patches fill I Know You Rider, Around And Around, Playing In The Band, Eyes Of The World and Let It Grow; this re-patches an earlier, less complete release [1]
- **gd1973-09-26.sbd.mtx.tobin.82879.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (65%-SBD/35%-AUD) [2]. Also: Chain: soundboard to master reel to DAT, played on a Sony R500, into Samplitude, then FLAC; transfers by Charlie Miller; Audience patches from Matt Smith and SIRMick fill several songs, including Rider, Playing, Eyes and Let It Grow [2]
- **gd1973-09-26.aud.tobin.80665.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: Unknown Audience [4]. Also: Audience tape came via SirMick from Chuck Diliberto, who got it from the Buffalo taper; The circulating soundboard had its own speed problems, so the Charlie Miller DAT version was used for patching [4]
- **gd73-09-26.sbd.brame.16155.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]. Also: The missing Playing in the Band can be found in the MP3 section of gdlive.com; Soundboard from reel to DAT to CD, patched with unknown audience source; converted to SHN and uploaded by Tripp [5][8]
